goal.statement: Explain to a friend why light cannot escape a black hole, and roughly where the boundary sits.
goal.audience: a curious adult, no physics past school

capstone.prompt: The Sun weighs about 2e30 kg. If it collapsed, how wide would its boundary be — and why won't it?
rubric: uses light speed as the limit

assumed: speed, distance and time in everyday terms

kcs.label: Gravity pulls harder the closer you are to the mass
misconceptions: gravity depends only on how big something looks

check.stem: You move twice as far from a planet's centre. The pull on you…
options: gets weaker
stays the same because you are still in its field
switches off once you leave the atmosphere
gets stronger because you have more room to fall
distractorSource: gravity depends only on how big something looks
gravity switches off in space
gravity switches off in space

kcs.label: Escape velocity is how fast you must go to get away and never fall back
misconceptions: any gravity well can be escaped given enough time
escape velocity is a speed limit rather than a threshold

check.stem: A rocket leaves Earth below escape velocity, with its engine off. What happens?
options: it falls back
it drifts away slowly
it stops at a fixed height
it cannot happen — nothing goes that slowly
distractorSource: any gravity well can be escaped given enough time
any gravity well can be escaped given enough time
escape velocity is a speed limit rather than a threshold

kcs.label: Escape velocity rises with more mass and falls with more distance
misconceptions: escape velocity depends on the escaping object's mass
escape velocity depends on the planet's size rather than its mass

check.stem: A feather and a cannonball both leave the same planet's surface. Their escape velocities are…
options: the same
lower for the feather
higher for the cannonball
impossible to compare
distractorSource: escape velocity depends on the escaping object's mass
escape velocity depends on the escaping object's mass
escape velocity depends on the planet's size rather than its mass

kcs.label: Light travels at one fixed speed, about 300,000 km per second
misconceptions: light speeds up when it is brighter
light's speed depends on the source's motion

check.stem: A torch on a moving train shines forward. The light travels at…
options: its usual speed
its usual speed plus the train's
faster because the beam is brighter
a speed that depends on the train
distractorSource: light's speed depends on the source's motion
light speeds up when it is brighter
light's speed depends on the source's motion

kcs.label: Nothing carrying information can travel faster than light
misconceptions: a fast enough rocket could outrun light
the limit is only about what we can currently build

check.stem: Why can't a signal outrun light?
options: nothing carrying information can go faster
we have not built a fast enough engine
it can, over short distances
only light itself is limited
distractorSource: the limit is only about what we can currently build
a fast enough rocket could outrun light
a fast enough rocket could outrun light

kcs.label: Where escape velocity reaches light speed, nothing inside can get out
misconceptions: the boundary is a solid surface
you could still escape from inside with a powerful enough engine

check.stem: What is special about the radius where escape velocity equals light speed?
options: nothing inside it can get out
it is a physical shell you could touch
a strong enough rocket could still leave
light slows down as it crosses it
distractorSource: the boundary is a solid surface
you could still escape from inside with a powerful enough engine
the boundary is a solid surface

kcs.label: Squeezing the same mass into a smaller ball raises escape velocity at its surface
misconceptions: squeezing something changes how much mass it has
only adding mass can raise escape velocity

check.stem: A planet shrinks but keeps all its mass. Escape velocity at the new surface…
options: goes up
stays the same — the mass did not change
goes down, there is less material to climb past
depends on how heavy you are
distractorSource: only adding mass can raise escape velocity
squeezing something changes how much mass it has
squeezing something changes how much mass it has

kcs.label: A black hole is mass squeezed inside its own no-escape radius
misconceptions: a black hole is a hole, an absence of stuff
black holes suck things in from any distance

check.stem: Swap the Sun for a black hole of exactly the same mass. Earth's orbit…
options: is unchanged
collapses inward immediately
widens because a hole has no mass
is pulled in from any distance
distractorSource: black holes suck things in from any distance
a black hole is a hole, an absence of stuff
black holes suck things in from any distance
